subject.title: fix(memory-core): honor private-network settings for OpenAI-compatible embeddings

question: Should configured OpenAI-compatible memory embeddings use the shared provider transport semantics where omission trusts only the exact configured origin, explicit false denies private access, and explicit true permits broader private-network access?
rationale: The patch correctly implements and proves all three states, but selecting the default trust and explicit-denial upgrade behavior is an intentional SSRF and compatibility policy choice.

options.title: Approve three-state contract
options.body: Land the shared resolver approach with the current exact-origin documentation and regression proof.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Make omitted policy fail closed so every private embedding endpoint requires explicit `allowPrivateNetwork: true`.

options.title: Use memory-specific policy
options.body: Introduce a separate memory trust setting despite creating a second source of network-policy truth.

recommendation.title: Approve three-state contract
recommendation.body: Land the shared resolver approach with the current exact-origin documentation and regression proof.
